paper.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
paper.central_claim: DEPS integrates event-triggered execution descriptions, LLM explanations and replanning with a trained horizon-based selector, robustly accomplishes more than70 open-world tasks and nearly doubles overall success versus LLM planner baselines with the same goal-conditioned controller.

Furthermore, it includes a goal $\textit{selector}$, which is a trainable module that ranks parallel candidate sub-goals based on the estimated steps of completion, consequently refining the initial plan. signatures.information: Task command, controller status, symbolic inventory/biome and game-state messages; Minecraft controller also uses visual and auxiliary state inputs.
signatures.operation: Event descriptor compresses execution failures; LLM explains why failure occurred and revises plan; controller executes translated subgoals.
signatures.conditions: Descriptor must expose relevant failure; LLM explanation must be causally useful; controller must support subgoal and parse its translation.
signatures.feedback: Inventory/event success or failure prompts diagnosis and replanning until task/round cap.
signatures.selection_rule: Replace local plan following event-triggered explanation; no accepted persistent harness update.
signatures.data: Minecraft BC controller on262 goals; examples in Appendix G overlap named evaluation tasks; repeated task episodes with random seeds.
signatures.persistence: Revised plan and dialogue retained only within current task context.
signatures.later_use: Subsequent subgoals of same episode; no verified cross-task learning claimed.
signatures.claimed_effect: Nearly doubled broad-task success and failure recovery.
signatures.failure_boundary: Privileged symbolic channels, token-capped extra calls, dead ends, hard-task zeros and perception/controller limitations.

signatures.information: Current observation and candidate goals with shared preconditions; controller-competence data from successful offline trajectories.
signatures.operation: Train goal-conditioned horizon predictor on remaining trajectory steps; rank parallel subgoals by predicted execution horizon and select easier/shorter ones.
signatures.conditions: Offline horizon labels must predict current controller efficiency; equivalent-precondition candidates must preserve task feasibility.
signatures.feedback: Observed progress leads to new candidates; selector is a trained component, not online RL or self-generated persistent improvement.
signatures.selection_rule: Predicted shorter horizon among currently comparable candidate goals.
signatures.data: Offline successful trajectories; distinct CLIP/MineCLIP/fixed/random selector comparisons; not planning-parameter training-free for whole stack.
signatures.persistence: Pretrained selector weights, fixed during reported task execution.
signatures.later_use: Reuse selector across tasks with the same supported controller/domain.
signatures.claimed_effect: DEP39.36→DEPS48.56 and stronger benefit on long efficiency-sensitive tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: No guarantee for unseen controller/task distributions; selector omitted in auxiliary domains.

gap.author_gap: Initial LLM plans contain long-horizon errors and ignore how difficult parallel subgoals are for the actual controller.
gap.checked_gap: Error diagnosis and competence-aware ordering are concrete residuals beyond feedback-only planning. However, the authors' broad suggestion that all earlier plans assume correctness is too strong: Inner Monologue already performs feedback-based planning.

lineage.method: Vanilla LLM planning, ProgPrompt/CaP program plans, Inner Monologue feedback, SayCan affordance weighting; learned goal-conditioned controllers
lineage.source_version: 2302.01560v3 Sec5/Appendix D descriptions; original adjacent versions not independently read/fixed here

gap.closest_adjacent: Inner Monologue supplies environment feedback; CaP and ProgPrompt structure plans. Residual proposed distinction is explicit failure explanation and horizon-ranked parallel goals, not feedback or decomposition in general.
gap.residue: Feedback alone need not correct the right causal error; plausible ordering may waste limited episode horizon.
gap.stakes: Controller failures and inefficient ordering compound in long multi-goal tasks.
gap.method_response: Descriptor→explain→revise loop plus offline-trained horizon selector.
gap.remaining_gap: Explanation content not isolated from extra compute; main baseline models differ; symbolic game-state channel and demonstration overlap limit generalization; hardest tasks remain rarely solved.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.reason: Fixed controller and DEP/DEPS help; main GPT/CoT/IM vs PP/CaP/ours use different backbones. Appendix C supplies within-model vanilla/DEPS comparisons.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.reason: Selector variants and replanning-round sweeps exist; explanation content is not isolated against equal-call same-context correction.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E03 (ablation, common_practice).** Report the harness or tool effect under at least two backbones of different strength. Several read papers find that tools and imposed structure help weak models and are neutral or harmful for strong ones. A gain measured on the teacher therefore does not predict the gain for a compact student. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.
expectations.reason: Appendix C Table19 tests vanilla/DEPS across Codex/GPT3/ChatGPT/GPT4; this is multi-backbone support, not token fairness.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.applies_when: any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.reason: 30 task trials, meta-category dispersions and per-task rates provided; uncertainty aggregation and unique catalog denominator not fully reconciled, no paired significance test.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E08 (reproducibility, common_practice).** State contamination and development-overlap caveats. Frontier 'zero-shot' describes how the model was used, not what it was trained on. Disclose whether the evaluation tasks were used during harness development, and whether ablations ran under a privileged action space that is not comparable to the benchmark protocol. — _applies when_ a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.
expectations.applies_when: a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.
expectations.reason: Game-state inputs, pretrained controller, prompts and task lists disclosed, but prompt/evaluation task overlap, no category exclusion and unknown foundation contamination limit held-out/zero-shot meaning.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E22 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Compare interfaces and harnesses at a matched interaction budget: the same caps on LLM calls, turns, wall-clock time and GPU. Disclose any asymmetry, such as uncapped turns or extra compute for tool runs, because budget endings drive many success differences. — _applies when_ a comparison between harnesses, interfaces or tool bundles with the model fixed.
expectations.applies_when: a comparison between harnesses, interfaces or tool bundles with the model fixed.
expectations.reason: Environment step caps and token-driven7–8 rounds disclosed; increasing rounds consumes extra model computation and no equal-call explanation control.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E05 (metric, common_practice).** Report cost alongside success: model calls, input and output tokens, wall-clock or per-call latency, and USD per episode or per solved task, including failed trials. Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.reason: Round/token capacity and step limits are inferable, but no total tokens/latency/USD including failed attempts and controller/selector training.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E19 (other, common_practice).** Real-robot claims need trial counts and success rates per task. Qualitative demonstrations, or success judged by a human operator without counts, do not support transfer claims. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness or harness-distilled student transfers to a physical robot or aerial vehicle.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness or harness-distilled student transfers to a physical robot or aerial vehicle.
expectations.reason: Tabletop/ALFWorld experiments are simulation, not repeated physical robot deployment.

claims.text: Nearly doubles overall success and robustly solves70+ tasks.
claims.setting: Minecraft/MineDojo with same BC controller, random worlds/spawns and task-dependent step caps
claims.baseline/control: GPT15.42, PP16.88, CoT18.89, IM21.64, CaP25.77, DEP39.36, DEPS48.56; main backbones not all matched
claims.data_budget: ≥30 trials/task; BC controller262 goals; more model rounds than vanilla; prompt demonstrations include evaluated task names
claims.selection_vs_test: No strict excluded task-category development holdout; random worlds are not independent harness-design/test separation
claims.result: DEPS48.56 aggregate vs CaP25.77; selector adds9.20pp over DEP; diamond0.59% and several hard per-task zeros.
claims.denominator: 30 executions/task stated; catalog task-count discrepancy71 vs numbering through76 unresolved
claims.counterevidence: Main backbone mismatch; hardest tasks not robust; inventory/GPS-like symbolic channels; explanation tokens unbalanced.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong average author-reported simulated gains with these tools/controllers; neither every task robustly solved nor explanation itself causally isolated.

claims.text: General interactive planning recipe extends beyond Minecraft.
claims.setting: ALFWorld and CLIPort tabletop simulation auxiliary studies
claims.baseline/control: ALFWorld DEP76 vs GPT10/GPT+replan52/IM30; tabletop DEP80 equals GPT80; different per-domain LLMs and selector omitted
claims.data_budget: ALFWorld10 tasks×5 trials; tabletop5 seen CLIPort tasks×5 seeds
claims.selection_vs_test: Domain-specific prompts/descriptors; tabletop tasks from training task families, not structural holdout
claims.result: Improvement in ALFWorld but no GPT advantage in tabletop; PickTwo ALFWorld task remains zero.
claims.counterevidence: No single unchanged harness/model/controller crossing domains; no real robot evidence.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Interactive recipe instantiates in multiple simulators, not measured generic transfer of a frozen full harness.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Under author-reported game-state feedback and a fixed BC controller, DEPS improves aggregate Minecraft task completion, with additional horizon-selection gains and repeated trials. Auxiliary ALFWorld supports the recipe, but tabletop equals GPT and hardest Minecraft tasks remain near zero.

G.reason: Two specific structural bottlenecks, plan repair and controller-aware ordering, are important; nearest feedback work already covers part of claimed gap and broader lineage not independently fixed.

M.reason: Event diagnosis and horizon ranking make distinguishable predictions and align with failure/efficiency; explanations and offline horizon fidelity remain hypotheses under privileged state.

X.reason: Descriptor/explainer/planner/controller and fixed-selector chain reconstructable, full prompts present; task/prompt bookkeeping and deployable information conditions limit complete execution assurance.

measurement.reason: Inventory goal criteria, repeated trials and environment task rates support closed-loop outcomes; privileged symbolic state and catalog discrepancies keep middle-band rather than unqualified verifier/transfer evidence.

causality.reason: Fixed-controller DEP/DEPS and Appendix19 within-model comparisons support contribution, but backbone, extra-replan-compute and non-isolated explanation remain material alternatives.

holdout.reason: Random world seeds and auxiliary domains add breadth but evaluated task names occur in prompts, selectors/controllers/domain prompts differ and symbolic channels are privileged; no clean held-out category/body gain.

statistics.reason: Repeated30 trials/task plus dispersions and full per-task rates expose hard-task zeros. Catalog/uncertainty aggregation and absence of paired CI prevent4.

cost.reason: Step and approximate token-driven round caps disclose a rough budget boundary, but added LLM and selector/controller cost not priced and explanation comparison not budget matched.
